calculators.formula_explanation:
Australian income tax is calculated using progressive ATO brackets for 2026/27: 0% up to $18,200 (tax-free threshold); 19% from $18,201–$45,000; 32.5% from $45,001–$135,000; 37% from $135,001–$190,000; 45% above $190,000.

The Low Income Tax Offset (LITO) reduces tax by up to $700 for incomes below $37,500, phasing out above that.

The Medicare Levy is 2% of taxable income (with a low-income reduction below ~$26,000). The Medicare Levy Surcharge adds 1%–1.5% if you earn above $93,000 and don't hold private hospital cover.

HECS/HELP compulsory repayments start at 1% when income exceeds $54,435, scaling up to 10% above $141,848. This reduces your take-home but also reduces your outstanding debt.

article_faq.question: What are the Australian income tax rates for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: For Australian tax residents in 2026/27: 0% on income up to $18,200 (tax-free threshold); 19 cents for each $1 between $18,201 and $45,000; 32.5 cents per $1 between $45,001 and $135,000; 37 cents per $1 between $135,001 and $190,000; and 45 cents per $1 above $190,000. These rates exclude the 2% Medicare Levy.

article_faq.question: When does the Medicare Levy Surcharge apply?
article_faq.answer: The Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS) applies if your income exceeds $93,000 (singles) and you don't have an appropriate level of private hospital cover. The surcharge rate is 1% for $93,001–$108,000, 1.25% for $108,001–$144,000, and 1.5% above $144,000. Getting private hospital cover is often cheaper than paying the surcharge.

article_faq.question: How are HECS/HELP repayments calculated in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Compulsory HECS/HELP repayments begin when your repayment income reaches $54,435. The rate starts at 1% and increases with income, reaching 10% above $141,848. Repayments are automatically withheld by your employer if you notify them. They reduce your HELP debt but are not tax deductible.

article_faq.question: What is the Low Income Tax Offset (LITO)?
article_faq.answer: The LITO reduces the amount of tax you pay if you're an Australian resident earning below $66,667. The maximum offset is $700 for incomes up to $37,500. It reduces by 5 cents for each dollar between $37,500 and $45,000, then by 1.5 cents per dollar from $45,000 to $66,667. Above $66,667, no offset applies.

article_faq.question: How much superannuation should my employer be paying?
article_faq.answer: From 1 July 2025, the Superannuation Guarantee (SG) rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings. Your employer must pay this on top of your salary into your nominated super fund. This is in addition to your gross salary shown above and is not included in take-home pay calculations.

inputs.name: private_health
inputs.label_native: Do you have Private Patient Hospital Cover?

calculators.formula_explanation: Gross Revenue minus allowable business expenses gives Gross Operating Profit. Deductions for home office (business % of home costs) and vehicle (business % of vehicle costs) reduce operating profit. Superannuation concessional contributions up to the $30,000 cap are tax-deductible for sole traders. Taxable Income is taxed using progressive ATO resident brackets. The Low Income Tax Offset (LITO) applies up to $66,667. The Small Business Income Tax Offset (SBITO) provides a tax discount of 16% on tax payable on business income, up to a maximum of $1,000 per year. The 2% Medicare Levy is added to determine total tax liability.

article_faq.question: What deductions can an Australian sole trader claim in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Sole traders can claim operating expenses, home office running costs (or standard hourly rate), vehicle expenses based on logbook percentage or cents-per-km method, professional subscriptions, insurance, and personal superannuation contributions up to the $30,000 concessional cap.

article_faq.question: How does the Small Business Income Tax Offset (SBITO) work?
article_faq.answer: The SBITO reduces the tax you pay on business income by up to $1,000 per year. The offset rate is 16% of the income tax payable on your net business income. The ATO automatically calculates this when you lodge your tax return.

article_faq.question: Can sole traders claim super contributions as a tax deduction?
article_faq.answer: Yes. Personal super contributions made by sole traders to an eligible super fund are tax-deductible up to the annual concessional contribution cap of $30,000 for 2026/27. You must submit a 'Notice of Intent to Claim' form to your super fund before lodging your tax return.

article_faq.question: When do sole traders pay PAYG Installments?
article_faq.answer: Once your tax return shows business and investment income generating tax payable above $4,000, the ATO will enter you into the PAYG Installment system, requiring quarterly payments towards your annual tax bill.

inputs.name: expected_return_pct
inputs.label_native: Expected Annual Return (% net of fees & tax)

calculators.formula_explanation: Employer Superannuation Guarantee (SG) contribution is set at 12% of salary (effective 1 July 2025). Total gross contributions equal SG (12%) plus voluntary salary sacrifice contributions. Concessional contributions are taxed at 15% upon entry into the fund (or 30% if taxable income plus concessional contributions exceed $250,000 under Division 293). The net annual contribution compounds annually alongside the existing balance at the specified net investment return rate: FV = PV * (1+r)^n + PMT * (((1+r)^n - 1) / r). Retirement drawdown is estimated using the 4% safe withdrawal rate.

article_faq.question: What is the Superannuation Guarantee (SG) rate for 2026?
article_faq.answer: The Super Guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings from 1 July 2025 onwards. Employers must pay this compulsory contribution into your super fund at least quarterly.

article_faq.question: How are super contributions taxed in Australia?
article_faq.answer: Concessional (pre-tax) contributions, including employer SG and salary sacrifice, are taxed at a concessional rate of 15% inside the super fund up to the annual cap of $30,000. Higher earners with income over $250,000 pay an additional 15% tax under Division 293.

article_faq.question: What is Division 293 tax?
article_faq.answer: Division 293 tax is an additional 15% tax levied on concessional super contributions for individuals whose income plus concessional contributions exceed $250,000 per year, bringing their total contribution tax rate to 30%.

article_faq.question: What is the concessional super contribution cap for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: The concessional contribution cap is $30,000 per financial year. Contributions above this cap are taxed at your marginal income tax rate.

calculators.description_native: Calculate property transfer stamp duty across all Australian states and territories. Factors in first home buyer exemptions and foreign buyer surcharges.
calculators.formula_explanation: Stamp duty (land transfer duty) is levied by Australian state and territory governments based on property purchase price. NSW: Standard scaled rates up to $1.168M, 5.5% above $1.168M. FHB: 100% duty exemption up to $800,000, sliding scale concession $800k–$1,000,000. VIC: Scaled rates up to 6.5%. FHB: 100% exemption up to $600,000, sliding scale $600k–$750,000. QLD: Scaled rates up to 5.75%. FHB: 100% exemption up to $700,000. WA: Scaled 1.9% to 5.15%. FHB exemption up to $450,000. SA: Scaled 1% to 5.5%. TAS: Scaled up to 4.5%. ACT: Abolished for eligible FHB under income cap, sliding scale for others. NT: Formula-based. Foreign purchasers pay an additional surcharge of 7%–9% depending on state.

article_faq.question: How much stamp duty do First Home Buyers pay in NSW?
article_faq.answer: Under the NSW First Home Buyers Assistance Scheme, first home buyers pay $0 stamp duty on homes valued up to $800,000. For homes between $800,000 and $1,000,000, a concessional sliding stamp duty rate applies.

article_faq.question: What is the First Home Buyer stamp duty threshold in Victoria?
article_faq.answer: In Victoria, first home buyers pay zero stamp duty on homes priced up to $600,000. A sliding discount applies for homes priced between $600,001 and $750,000.

article_faq.question: Do foreign buyers pay extra stamp duty in Australia?
article_faq.answer: Yes. Foreign buyers are subject to a foreign purchaser surcharge in addition to standard stamp duty: 8% in NSW, VIC, and TAS; 8% in QLD; 7% in WA and SA.

article_faq.question: When is property stamp duty payable?
article_faq.answer: Stamp duty is typically due at settlement or within 30 to 90 days of signing the contract, depending on the state or territory.

calculators.description_native: Calculate compulsory HECS/HELP repayments and payoff timelines for 2026/27. Factors in ATO repayment income thresholds and annual CPI indexation.
calculators.formula_explanation: Compulsory HELP repayments are calculated based on your total repayment income using progressive ATO brackets starting at $54,435 (1%) up to $141,848 (10%). Remaining HELP debt is indexed annually on 1 June using the lower of CPI or WPI (estimated ~3.8% for 2026). In each projected year: compulsory and voluntary repayments reduce the balance first, and annual indexation is applied to the remaining balance on 1 June. Repayments continue until the debt balance reaches $0.

article_faq.question: What is the minimum income threshold for HECS/HELP repayments in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: For the 2026/27 tax year, the compulsory HECS/HELP repayment threshold begins at $54,435. Incomes below this amount require $0 compulsory repayment.

article_faq.question: How are HECS/HELP debts indexed in Australia?
article_faq.answer: HELP debts are indexed annually on 1 June. Under recent legislation, indexation is calculated using the lower of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or Wage Price Index (WPI) to prevent excessive indexation.

article_faq.question: Are HECS/HELP repayments tax-deductible?
article_faq.answer: No, compulsory and voluntary HELP debt repayments are made with after-tax dollars and are not tax-deductible.

article_faq.question: Should I make voluntary repayments on my HECS/HELP debt?
article_faq.answer: Voluntary repayments directly reduce your balance and avoid future indexation. However, because HELP loans carry no interest (only indexation), many financial advisers suggest prioritizing high-interest debts before making voluntary HELP payments.
